summary: Renewed clashes on the disputed Cambodia-Thailand border have killed at least 13 people, including Thai soldiers and Cambodian civilians, and displaced over 500,000 civilians. The displaced are taking shelter in pagodas, schools, and other safe havens. The fighting, the deadliest since a truce in July, has expanded to five provinces, with both sides blaming each other, and led to Cambodia's withdrawal from the SEA Games hosted by Thailand.

summary: More than half a million people have been forced to flee to safe shelters amid deadly border clashes between Thailand and Cambodia. summary: Thailand formally notified the UN Security Council on December 9 that it is exercising its right to self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter following what it described as "unprovoked armed attacks" by Cambodia across five Thai border provinces. Bangkok's UN envoy detailed a series of incidents, accusing Cambodia of deliberately targeting Thai civilians and infrastructure with heavy weaponry, violating the UN Charter, and engaging in disinformation. Thailand demanded Cambodia accept full responsibility and cease all hostile acts, stating its military measures are necessary, proportional, and aimed solely at neutralizing imminent danger.

Thailand demanded Cambodia accept full responsibility and cease all hostile acts, stating its military measures are necessary, proportional, and aimed solely at neutralizing imminent danger.
summaryKh: នៅថ្ងៃទី 9 ខែធ្នូ ប្រទេសថៃបានជូនដំណឹងជាផ្លូវការទៅកាន់ក្រុមប្រឹក្សាសន្តិសុខអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិ (UNSC) ថាខ្លួនកំពុងប្រើប្រាស់សិទ្ធិការពារខ្លួនក្រោមមាត្រា 51 នៃធម្មនុញ្ញអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិ បន្ទាប់ពីអ្វីដែលខ្លួនបានហៅថា «ការវាយប្រហារដោយអាវុធដែលគ្មានការបង្កហេតុ» ដោយកម្ពុជានៅទូទាំងខេត្តព្រំដែនថៃ 5។ បេសកជន UN របស់ទីក្រុងបាងកកបានរៀបរាប់លម្អិតអំពីឧបទ្ទវហេតុមួយចំនួន ដោយចោទប្រកាន់កម្ពុជាថាបានកំណត់គោលដៅដោយចេតនាលើជនស៊ីវិល និងហេដ្ឋារចនាសម្ព័ន្ធថៃដោយអាវុធធុនធ្ងន់ រំលោភធម្មនុញ្ញអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិ និងចូលរួមក្នុងការបំភ័ន្តព័ត៌មាន។ ប្រទេសថៃបានទាមទារឱ្យកម្ពុជាទទួលខុសត្រូវពេញលេញ និងបញ្ឈប់រាល់អំពើអរិភាព ដោយបញ្ជាក់ថាវិធានការយោធារបស់ខ្លួនគឺចាំបាច់ សមាមាត្រ និងមានគោលបំណងតែមួយគត់ដើម្បីបន្សាបគ្រោះថ្នាក់ដែលជិតកើតឡើង។

summary: Cambodia has formally escalated the border dispute to the UN Security Council, submitting a letter on December 10 requesting urgent action against Thailand's "unprovoked and escalating armed attacks." The Cambodian Permanent Representative accused Thai forces of violating the UN Charter and international humanitarian law by using heavy weapons, warplanes, and toxic smoke in attacks that allegedly extended into civilian areas and damaged protected heritage sites.
summaryEn: Cambodia has formally escalated the border dispute to the UN Security Council, submitting a letter on December 10 requesting urgent action against Thailand's "unprovoked and escalating armed attacks." The Cambodian Permanent Representative accused Thai forces of violating the UN Charter and international humanitarian law by using heavy weapons, warplanes, and toxic smoke in attacks that allegedly extended into civilian areas and damaged protected heritage sites.
summaryKh: កម្ពុជាបានបង្កើនវិវាទព្រំដែនទៅកាន់ក្រុមប្រឹក្សាសន្តិសុខអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិជាផ្លូវការ ដោយបានដាក់លិខិតមួយនៅថ្ងៃទី 10 ខែធ្នូ ដើម្បីស្នើសុំសកម្មភាពបន្ទាន់ប្រឆាំងនឹង "ការវាយប្រហារដោយអាវុធដែលកើនឡើង និងគ្មានការបង្ករឿង" របស់កងកម្លាំងថៃ។ តំណាងអចិន្ត្រៃយ៍កម្ពុជាបានចោទប្រកាន់កងកម្លាំងថៃថាបានបំពានធម្មនុញ្ញអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិ និងច្បាប់មនុស្សធម៌អន្តរជាតិ ដោយប្រើប្រាស់អាវុធធុនធ្ងន់ យន្តហោះចម្បាំង និងផ្សែងពុលក្នុងការវាយប្រហារដែលត្រូវបានចោទប្រកាន់ថាបានពង្រីកដល់តំបន់ស៊ីវិល និងបំផ្លាញទីតាំងបេតិកភណ្ឌដែលត្រូវបានការពារ។
summaryTh: กัมพูชาได้ยกระดับข้อพิพาทชายแดนขึ้นสู่คณะมนตรีความมั่นคงแห่งสหประชาชาติอย่างเป็นทางการ โดยยื่นหนังสือเมื่อวันที่ 10 ธันวาคม เพื่อขอให้ดำเนินการเร่งด่วนต่อ "การโจมตีด้วยอาวุธที่เพิ่มขึ้นและไม่มีการยั่วยุ" ของกองทัพไทย ผู้แทนถาวรกัมพูชากล่าวหากองทัพไทยว่าละเมิดกฎบัตรสหประชาชาติและกฎหมายมนุษยธรรมระหว่างประเทศ โดยใช้อาวุธหนัก เครื่องบินรบ และควันพิษในการโจมตีที่อ้างว่าขยายไปยังพื้นที่พลเรือนและสร้างความเสียหายต่อแหล่งมรดกที่ได้รับการคุ้มครอง

summary: An analysis piece arguing that ASEAN's current passive role is dangerous and insufficient. It calls for the immediate activation of the ASEAN High Council under the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (TAC) and proposes the appointment of Nobel Peace Laureate José Ramos-Horta to lead a mediation effort. The article states that quiet bilateral diplomacy has failed amidst rising casualties and hardening nationalist sentiment, underscoring the need for a stronger regional intervention.

The article states that quiet bilateral diplomacy has failed amidst rising casualties and hardening nationalist sentiment, underscoring the need for a stronger regional intervention.
summaryKh: អត្ថបទនេះលើកឡើងថា តួនាទីអសកម្មរបស់អាស៊ានគឺមានគ្រោះថ្នាក់ ហើយអំពាវនាវឱ្យមានការដាក់ឱ្យដំណើរការក្រុមប្រឹក្សាជាន់ខ្ពស់អាស៊ាន (ASEAN High Council) ក្រោមសន្ធិសញ្ញាមិត្តភាព និងកិច្ចសហប្រតិបត្តិការ (TAC)។ វាស្នើឱ្យតែងតាំងលោក José Ramos-Horta អ្នកឈ្នះរង្វាន់ណូបែលសន្តិភាព ដើម្បីដឹកនាំកិច្ចខិតខំប្រឹងប្រែងសម្របសម្រួល ដោយលើកហេតុផលថា យុទ្ធសាស្ត្រការទូតទ្វេភាគីបែបស្ងាត់ៗបានបរាជ័យចំពេលដែលមានការកើនឡើងនៃចំនួនអ្នកស្លាប់ ការផ្លាស់ទីលំនៅ និងមនោសញ្ចេតនាជាតិនិយមដែលកាន់តែរឹងមាំឡើង។
summaryTh: บทความนี้โต้แย้งว่าบทบาทที่นิ่งเฉยของอาเซียนเป็นอันตราย และเรียกร้องให้มีการเปิดใช้สภาสูงอาเซียนภายใต้สนธิสัญญามิตรภาพและความร่วมมือในเอเชียตะวันออกเฉียงใต้ (TAC) โดยเสนอให้แต่งตั้งนาย José Ramos-Horta ผู้ได้รับรางวัลโนเบลสาขาสันติภาพเป็นผู้นำการไกล่เกลี่ย เนื่องจากวิธีการทางการทูตทวิภาคีอย่างเงียบ ๆ ได้ล้มเหลวท่ามกลางจำนวนผู้เสียชีวิตและการพลัดถิ่นที่เพิ่มขึ้น และความรู้สึกชาตินิยมที่แข็งกร้าวขึ้น

summary: Cambodia has formally asked the UN Security Council for urgent action, describing Thailand's actions as “a series of unprovoked and escalating armed attacks” that violate the UN Charter and international humanitarian law. In a letter, Cambodia's Permanent Representative to the UN requested the council to condemn Thailand's actions and demand an immediate cessation of military operations.

In a letter, Cambodia's Permanent Representative to the UN requested the council to condemn Thailand's actions and demand an immediate cessation of military operations.

summaryTh: กัมพูชาได้ยื่นคำร้องอย่างเป็นทางการต่อคณะมนตรีความมั่นคงแห่งสหประชาชาติเพื่อขอให้ดำเนินการเร่งด่วน โดยบรรยายถึงการกระทำของไทยว่าเป็น “ชุดของการโจมตีด้วยอาวุธที่ไม่มีการยั่วยุและทวีความรุนแรงขึ้น” ซึ่งละเมิดกฎบัตร UN และกฎหมายมนุษยธรรมระหว่างประเทศ ในจดหมาย ผู้แทนถาวรของกัมพูชาประจำ UN เรียกร้องให้คณะมนตรีประณามการกระทำของไทยและเรียกร้องให้ยุติปฏิบัติการทางทหารทันที

summary: The intensifying border fighting, which has displaced over half a million people, is now raising concerns for iconic cultural heritage sites. UNESCO called for the urgent protection of sites like Preah Vihear Temple and shared the geographical coordinates of World Heritage sites with all parties to avoid potential damage. At least 19 people have been killed so far, including 10 people in Cambodia and 9 in Thailand (8 soldiers, 1 civilian, with a later mention of 3 civilians).

UNESCO called for the urgent protection of sites like Preah Vihear Temple and shared the geographical coordinates of World Heritage sites with all parties to avoid potential damage. summary: The U.S. Embassy in Cambodia issued a security alert on December 12, 2025, monitoring the ongoing conflict along the Cambodia-Thailand border. summary: Both Thailand and Cambodia have escalated their diplomatic confrontation to the United Nations, each filing formal protest letters accusing the other of being the aggressor and violating the UN Charter and international humanitarian law. Thailand's letter cited one soldier killed and 18 injured, and Cambodia's letter accused Thailand of using 'toxic smoke' and violating a 24-hour restraint. The article also notes Pope Leo's call for an immediate ceasefire and resumption of dialogue.

summary: Renewed fighting, which has killed nearly a dozen people, over the Preah Vihear Temple border area highlights the dangers of unresolved historical conflicts rooted in colonial-era maps. The article suggests that both governments are leaning on nationalist sentiment to shore up domestic support ahead of the 2026 Thai election and for Hun Sen to reassert himself in Cambodian politics. It criticizes ASEAN's limited capacity to enforce lasting peace, calling for an independent observer mission and a neutral demarcation process based on existing ICJ rulings to resolve the underlying border dispute.

summaryTh: การต่อสู้ครั้งใหม่ที่ทำให้มีผู้เสียชีวิตเกือบ 12 ราย เหนือพื้นที่ชายแดนปราสาทพระวิหาร เน้นย้ำถึงอันตรายของความขัดแย้งทางประวัติศาสตร์ที่ยังไม่ได้รับการแก้ไขซึ่งมีรากฐานมาจากแผนที่ยุคอาณานิคม บทความนี้ชี้ให้เห็นว่าทั้งสองรัฐบาลกำลังพึ่งพาความรู้สึกชาตินิยมเพื่อเสริมสร้างการสนับสนุนในประเทศก่อนการเลือกตั้งของไทยในปี 2569 และเพื่อให้ฮุน เซน กลับมามีบทบาททางการเมืองในกัมพูชาอีกครั้ง บทความวิจารณ์ขีดความสามารถที่จำกัดของอาเซียนในการบังคับใช้สันติภาพที่ยั่งยืน และเรียกร้องให้มีคณะผู้สังเกตการณ์ที่เป็นกลางและกระบวนการปักปันเขตแดนที่เป็นกลางโดยอิงจากการตัดสินของศาลยุติธรรมระหว่างประเทศ (ICJ) ที่มีอยู่เพื่อแก้ไขข้อพิพาทชายแดนที่เป็นต้นเหตุ

summary: US President Donald Trump announced on social media that Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet agreed to renew a ceasefire, effective Friday evening, reverting to the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord terms. The truce follows days of deadly clashes and Trump credited Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim for his crucial mediating role, though neither side immediately confirmed the agreement.

summary: Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced he will dissolve parliament to clear the way for early elections within 45-60 days due to political deadlock. This internal political turmoil coincides with the ongoing fierce border conflict with Cambodia, which has resulted in at least 20 deaths and nearly 200 injuries, although Anutin insisted the elections would not affect military operations along the frontier.

summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs expressed concern over the damage caused to the Preah Vihear temple complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, following the Thailand-Cambodia border clashes. summary: US President Donald Trump announced on his social media that Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul and Cambodian PM Hun Manet agreed to 'CEASE all shooting effective this evening' and return to the original Peace Accord. summary: US President Donald Trump announced on social media that Thailand and Cambodia agreed to a ceasefire to halt renewed border fighting that has displaced approximately 700,000 people and killed at least 23. The agreement, facilitated with the help of Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim, aims to return to the original US-brokered peace accord. Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim, the current ASEAN chair, separately affirmed plans to convene a Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting to assess the crisis.

summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim urged Thailand and Cambodia to cease all hostilities from the night of Dec 13. summaryTh: การสู้รบอย่างหนักยังคงดำเนินไปในช่วงเช้าวันเสาร์ โดยเจ้าหน้าที่ไทยออกมาโต้แย้งคำกล่าวของประธานาธิบดีโดนัลด์ ทรัมป์ ของสหรัฐฯ ที่อ้างว่าเขาได้เป็นตัวกลางในการบรรลุข้อตกลงหยุดยิงแล้ว รัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศสียสักดิ์ พวงเกตุแก้ว กล่าวว่าคำพูดของทรัมป์ "ไม่ได้สะท้อนความเข้าใจที่ถูกต้องของสถานการณ์" ทั้งสองฝ่ายรายงานการยิงปืนใหญ่และการโจมตีทางอากาศต่อเนื่อง ทำให้มีพลเรือนบาดเจ็บ 2 รายจากจรวด BM-21 ยอดผู้เสียชีวิตที่ได้รับการยืนยันในสัปดาห์นี้มีมากกว่า 20 ราย และประชาชนหลายแสนคนต้องพลัดถิ่น

summary: Caretaker Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul publicly vowed on Saturday to 'continue to perform military actions' against Cambodia, directly contradicting President Donald Trump’s announcement that a new ceasefire had been brokered. Anutin stated there was 'no agreement on halting anything' with Cambodia. Meanwhile, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet welcomed a separate ceasefire proposal by Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim, which included an ASEAN observer team and US satellite monitoring. Clashes were reported across seven border provinces on Saturday, with heavy weapon fire continuing.

Anutin stated there was 'no agreement on halting anything' with Cambodia. Meanwhile, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet welcomed a separate ceasefire proposal by Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim, which included an ASEAN observer team and US satellite monitoring. Clashes were reported across seven border provinces on Saturday, with heavy weapon fire continuing.

summary: Heavy fighting continued on Saturday after President Donald Trump claimed he had brokered a new ceasefire. Thai officials, however, explicitly denied agreeing to any truce. The Thai Foreign Minister expressed disappointment that Trump’s remarks did not reflect an accurate understanding of Thailand’s position.

summary: Cambodia announced the immediate suspension of all entry and exit movements at its border crossings with Thailand on Saturday, following Bangkok's denial of US President Trump's claim of a truce. The renewed clashes have displaced about half a million people and resulted in at least 25 deaths this week, including four Thai soldiers killed on Saturday. Both sides are trading accusations over attacks on civilians.

summary: Thailand's Ministry of Defence reported 15 Thai soldiers killed and 270 wounded, along with 7 Thai civilian deaths, since December 7. In response to what it called Thai 'acts of aggression,' Cambodia's Interior Ministry announced the indefinite closure of all land border crossings with Thailand. The ongoing fighting in disputed areas has displaced over 263,000 people on the Thai side, raising fears of a prolonged conflict.

summary: Thailand declared a curfew in its southeastern Trat province on Sunday and is discussing blocking fuel exports to Cambodia amid the escalation of fighting, which has spread to coastal areas. The conflict has displaced hundreds of thousands of people, with casualties reported on both sides.

summary: Cambodia shut all its border crossings with Thailand on Saturday (Dec 13) after Bangkok denied US President Donald Trump's claim that a truce had been agreed to halt days of deadly fighting. Thailand's Prime Minister reiterated that no ceasefire had been reached and operations would continue. The violence, stemming from a colonial-era dispute, has displaced around half a million people, and at least 25 people were reported dead that week, including four Thai soldiers killed on Saturday.
summaryEn: Cambodia shut all its border crossings with Thailand on Saturday (Dec 13) after Bangkok denied US President Donald Trump's claim that a truce had been agreed to halt days of deadly fighting. Thailand's Prime Minister reiterated that no ceasefire had been reached and operations would continue. The violence, stemming from a colonial-era dispute, has displaced around half a million people, and at least 25 people were reported dead that week, including four Thai soldiers killed on Saturday.

summary: Thailand's military launched a new offensive on Sunday in Trat province to 'reclaim sovereign territory,' a move that spurns recent mediation efforts. Cambodia responded by announcing the closure of all its border crossings with Thailand. The ongoing violence, stemming from a long-running colonial-era border dispute, has left at least 25 soldiers and civilians dead and displaced over half a million people.

Cambodia responded by announcing the closure of all its border crossings with Thailand. The ongoing violence, stemming from a long-running colonial-era border dispute, has left at least 25 soldiers and civilians dead and displaced over half a million people.

summary: Renewed border clashes between Cambodia and Thailand entered a second week on Sunday, December 14, with Thai officials denying US President Donald Trump's claim that a truce had been agreed upon. The conflict, rooted in a colonial-era dispute, has displaced around 800,000 people. Both sides blame the other for instigating the fighting, which has officially killed at least 25 people, including Thai soldiers and Cambodian civilians.

summary: Thailand declared a curfew in its southeastern Trat province as fighting with Cambodia spread to coastal areas near a disputed border region, two days after US President Trump claimed a ceasefire was agreed upon. A Thai Defence Ministry spokesman confirmed continuous clashes and stated Thailand is open to a diplomatic solution, but Cambodia must cease hostilities first. The curfew covers five districts, excluding tourist islands, and follows reports of Thai forces destroying a bridge used by Cambodia to transport heavy weapons.

summary: Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through its spokesperson, laid out three conditions for a ceasefire, insisting that Cambodia must declare it first, ensure it happens in practice and is sustained, and cooperate seriously on landmine clearance. summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced the postponement of the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting (AMM) concerning the Cambodia-Thailand border tensions, stating the delay is to ensure everything is 'properly in place.' He continues to appeal to both sides to stop the fighting and remains in virtual contact with them daily.
summaryEn: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced on Monday that the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting (AMM) concerning the Cambodia-Thailand border tensions has been postponed from December 16 to December 22. The postponement was requested to ensure everything is "properly in place" for the meeting. Additionally, the report mentions that Thailand's military has designated the Gulf of Thailand as a high-risk area to cut off potential sea routes for military supplies to Cambodia, emphasizing it is a safety precaution that does not affect third-country vessels.

summary: Heavy combat between Thailand and Cambodia entered a second week. Cambodia claims that Thai F-16 fighter jets dropped two bombs near camps for displaced persons, with one incident targeting a bridge over 70km inside Cambodian territory near Siem Reap. Thailand did not comment, and independent verification is difficult. More than two dozen people have been officially reported killed and over half a million displaced.

summary: This analysis piece argues that the renewed border fighting between Thailand and Cambodia, the most serious since July, exposes the fragility of ceasefire diplomacy and the volatility of colonial-era disputes. It notes that the collapse of the US-brokered ceasefire was due to its failure to resolve the core issue—competing interpretations of the 1907 colonial map—and the lack of a robust monitoring or enforcement mechanism.

summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting, intended to address the escalating Thailand-Cambodia border conflict, has been postponed from December 16 to December 22 at Thailand's request. The move is part of Malaysia's attempt to reassert ASEAN's role in resolving the crisis, amid skepticism over the bloc's efficacy after failed mediation attempts by external actors.
summaryEn: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting, intended to address the escalating Thailand-Cambodia border conflict, has been postponed from December 16 to December 22 at Thailand's request. The report highlights that the conflict has expanded across the 817-kilometer border, involving heavy weapons and jet airstrikes from the Thai side, displacing around half a million people, and exposing the fragility of previous ceasefire efforts.

summary: This article analyzes the role of China's less prominent, quiet diplomacy in the July 2025 ceasefire, contrasting it with the high-profile pressure from the US. summary: Heavy fighting along the border has forced the closure of 1,039 schools in Cambodia across six provinces, affecting nearly 243,000 students. summary: This article summarizes international reactions to the renewed Thailand-Cambodia conflict. It notes US President Trump's claim of again helping to end the fighting; China's expression of deep concern over casualties and call for restraint; Malaysia's role as ASEAN Chair in urging a ceasefire and postponing a special meeting; France's call for both sides to honor previous agreements; and Russia's call for restraint while denying reports of Russian mercenaries fighting with Cambodian forces.

summary: Thailand has moved to block fuel shipments from reaching Cambodia as the border conflict intensifies, with over 500,000 people now displaced. Experts suggest domestic political pressure and the upcoming election may be driving the Thai government's firm stance in the conflict.

summary: Thailand insists that any move towards a ceasefire must begin with a unilateral declaration from Cambodia, according to Thai foreign ministry. Cambodia, meanwhile, claims Thai airstrikes are reaching deeper into its territory, hitting targets within 80km of the Angkor Wat tourism hotspot and taking a toll on tourism. The renewed conflict, sparked on December 7, continues with dozens killed and about 800,000 people displaced on both sides.

summaryTh: กระทรวงการต่างประเทศไทยยืนกรานว่าการเคลื่อนไหวสู่การหยุดยิงใดๆ จะต้องเริ่มต้นด้วยการประกาศฝ่ายเดียวจากกัมพูชา ขณะที่กัมพูชาอ้างว่าการโจมตีทางอากาศของไทยลึกเข้ามาในดินแดนของตน โดยโดนเป้าหมายในระยะ 80 กม. จากแหล่งท่องเที่ยวสำคัญอย่างนครวัด และส่งผลกระทบต่อการท่องเที่ยว ความขัดแย้งที่ปะทุขึ้นอีกครั้งเมื่อวันที่ 7 ธันวาคมยังคงดำเนินต่อไป โดยมีผู้เสียชีวิตหลายสิบคนและมีผู้พลัดถิ่นประมาณ 800,000 คนทั้งสองฝ่าย

summary: Reporting indicates that Cambodia has significantly modernized its military with Chinese equipment, including multiple rocket launchers and 'fifth-generation' anti-tank guided missiles (GAM-102LR) recently seized by Thai forces at Hill 500. summary: This neutral analysis highlights the fundamental map dispute fueling the current conflict: the 1907 French 'Annex I map' used by Cambodia versus the natural watershed line claimed by Thailand. The dispute focuses on three key Hindu temples—Preah Vihear (Khao Phra Viharn), Ta Moan Thom (Ta Muen Thom), and Ta Khwai (Prasat Ta Krabey). While the 1962 ICJ ruling awarded Preah Vihear to Cambodia, it left surrounding territory ill-defined, allowing nationalist narratives in both countries to exploit cartographic ambiguities during domestic political crises.
summaryEn: This neutral analysis highlights the fundamental map dispute fueling the current conflict: the 1907 French 'Annex I map' used by Cambodia versus the natural watershed line claimed by Thailand. The dispute focuses on three key Hindu temples—Preah Vihear (Khao Phra Viharn), Ta Moan Thom (Ta Muen Thom), and Ta Khwai (Prasat Ta Krabey). While the 1962 ICJ ruling awarded Preah Vihear to Cambodia, it left surrounding territory ill-defined, allowing nationalist narratives in both countries to exploit cartographic ambiguities during domestic political crises.
summaryKh: ការវិភាគដោយអព្យាក្រឹតនេះបានលើកឡើងពីជម្លោះផែនទីជាមូលដ្ឋានដែលបង្កឱ្យមានជម្លោះនាពេលបច្ចុប្បន្ន៖ 'ផែនទីឧបសម្ព័ន្ធទី 1' របស់បារាំងឆ្នាំ 1907 ដែលប្រើប្រាស់ដោយកម្ពុជា ធៀបនឹងខ្សែបន្ទាត់បែងចែកទឹកតាមធម្មជាតិដែលទាមទារដោយថៃ។ ជម្លោះនេះផ្តោតលើប្រាសាទបុរាណសំខាន់ៗចំនួនបីគឺ ប្រាសាទព្រះវិហារ ប្រាសាទតាមឿនធំ និងប្រាសាទតាខ្មៅ (ប្រាសាទតាក្របី)។ ទោះបីជាសាលក្រមរបស់ ICJ ឆ្នាំ 1962 បានកាត់សេចក្តីឱ្យប្រាសាទព្រះវិហារទៅកម្ពុជាក៏ដោយ ប៉ុន្តែវាបានទុកឱ្យទឹកដីជុំវិញមិនមានការកំណត់ច្បាស់លាស់ ដែលអនុញ្ញាតឱ្យមនោគមវិជ្ជាជាតិនិយមនៅក្នុងប្រទេសទាំងពីរទាញយកផលប្រយោជន៍ពីភាពមិនច្បាស់លាស់នៃផែនទីក្នុងអំឡុងពេលវិបត្តិវិបត្តិនយោបាយក្នុងស្រុក។
summaryTh: การวิเคราะห์ที่เป็นกลางนี้เน้นย้ำถึงข้อพิพาทเรื่องแผนที่ซึ่งเป็นชนวนเหตุของความขัดแย้งในปัจจุบัน ได้แก่ 'แผนที่ผนวก 1' (Annex I map) ของฝรั่งเศสปี 1907 ที่กัมพูชาใช้ อ้างอิงกับแนวสันปันน้ำตามธรรมชาติที่ไทยยึดถือ ข้อพิพาทมุ่งเป้าไปที่ปราสาทหินสามแห่ง ได้แก่ พระวิหาร (เขาพระวิหาร), ตาเมือนธม และตาควาย (ปราสาทตากระบือ) แม้ว่าคำตัดสินของศาลโลกปี 1962 จะตัดสินให้ปราสาทพระวิหารเป็นของกัมพูชา แต่ทิ้งพื้นที่รอบข้างไว้โดยไม่มีการกำหนดขอบเขตที่ชัดเจน ทำให้กระแสชาตินิยมในทั้งสองประเทศสามารถนำความคลุมเครือของแผนที่มาใช้ประโยชน์ในช่วงวิกฤตการเมืองในประเทศได้

summary: Military engagements have entered their 11th consecutive day, with the combined death toll reaching at least 52. Thai authorities report 19 soldiers and 16 civilians killed, while Cambodia reports 17 civilian deaths. Over 700,000 people have been displaced. Despite international mediation attempts, Thailand has set a condition that Cambodia must be the first to announce a credible ceasefire.

Despite international mediation attempts, Thailand has set a condition that Cambodia must be the first to announce a credible ceasefire.

summary: Thailand's Defense Ministry announced on Wednesday that the latest round of conflict has left at least 19 Thai soldiers and 19 Thai civilians dead. Over 270,000 people have been displaced. The ministry's spokesperson, Surasant Kongsiri, stated that Cambodia used heavy weapons for attacks in border areas from Tuesday night into early Wednesday morning.

summary: An analysis of the reignited conflict since December 7, describing it as one of the most intense Southeast Asian confrontations in decades. summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that Thailand and Cambodia have agreed to the deployment of an ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to monitor the border situation. The fighting has expanded across various sectors of the 817-kilometer border, involving Thai F-16 and Gripen jet airstrikes as well as Cambodian rocket fire. While Cambodia reported calm in some provinces, Thailand maintains that clashes are ongoing in Surin and Sisaket, claiming to be targeting transnational criminal networks.

summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk expressed deep alarm over reports of fighter jets, drones, and artillery striking areas near villages and cultural sites. He stated that approximately 750,000 people have fled their homes since fighting reignited on December 7. The UN noted that strikes have reportedly hit casino complexes and suspected scam centers in Cambodia, putting trafficked foreign nationals at further risk. Türk urged both sides to return to dialogue, citing their 'commitment to human rights' and shared history.

summary: Recent military actions by Thailand have expanded beyond traditional border disputes to include strikes on casinos and hotels in Cambodia allegedly linked to cross-border online fraud. Analysts suggest these strikes reflect Bangkok's dissatisfaction with previous peace deals. Despite recent U.S. attempts to broker a ceasefire using tariff threats, the conflict has only intensified, underscoring that trade-based diplomacy may be insufficient to resolve the deep-seated territorial and security issues between the two nations. China has also expressed 'deep concern' over the escalation.

summary: Thai fighter jets dropped three bombs in Poipet, a major casino hub, on Thursday morning. The Thai Air Force stated the strike destroyed a 'logistics center' used to store rockets, while Cambodian officials reported damage to a warehouse and two civilian injuries. The conflict has now killed at least 21 people in Thailand and 18 in Cambodia.

summary: On December 18, Thai fighter jets dropped three bombs in the Cambodian city of Poipet, hitting a building Thailand described as a "logistics centre" for rockets. Cambodia's Interior Ministry stated the attack damaged a warehouse and injured two civilians. The conflict has reportedly killed 21 in Thailand and 18 in Cambodia this month. China is sending a special envoy to both nations for "shuttle diplomacy" as ASEAN plans emergency talks for December 22.

Cambodia's Interior Ministry stated the attack damaged a warehouse and injured two civilians. The conflict has reportedly killed 21 in Thailand and 18 in Cambodia this month. China is sending a special envoy to both nations for "shuttle diplomacy" as ASEAN plans emergency talks for December 22.
summaryKh: នៅថ្ងៃទី 18 ខែធ្នូ យន្តហោះចម្បាំងថៃបានទម្លាក់គ្រាប់បែកចំនួនបីគ្រាប់ក្នុងទីក្រុងប៉ោយប៉ែត ប្រទេសកម្ពុជា ដោយបានវាយប្រហារលើអាគារមួយដែលភាគីថៃពណ៌នាថាជា "មជ្ឈមណ្ឌលភស្តុភារ" សម្រាប់គ្រាប់រ៉ុក្កែត។ ក្រសួងមហាផ្ទៃកម្ពុជាបានថ្លែងថា ការវាយប្រហារនេះបានធ្វើឱ្យខូចខាតឃ្លាំងមួយ និងធ្វើឱ្យជនស៊ីវិលពីរនាក់រងរបួស។ ជម្លោះនេះត្រូវបានរាយការណ៍ថាបានសម្លាប់មនុស្ស 21 នាក់ក្នុងប្រទេសថៃ និង 18 នាក់ក្នុងប្រទេសកម្ពុជានៅក្នុងខែនេះ។ ប្រទេសចិនកំពុងបញ្ជូនប្រេសិតពិសេសទៅកាន់ប្រទេសទាំងពីរសម្រាប់ "ការទូតចរចា" ខណៈដែលអាស៊ានគ្រោងនឹងបើកការចរចាបន្ទាន់នៅថ្ងៃទី 22 ខែធ្នូ។

summary: Cambodia's defense ministry alleged that Thai forces bombed the border casino town of Poipet, a major economic hub, on December 18. This escalation occurred as international powers, including China and Malaysia, stepped up diplomatic efforts to halt the fighting. China announced it was sending a special envoy for a 'shuttle-diplomacy' trip to bridge the gaps between the two nations as foreign nations pressured both sides to restore the truce.

summaryKh: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិកម្ពុជាបានចោទប្រកាន់ថា កងកម្លាំងថៃបានទម្លាក់គ្រាប់បែកលើក្រុងកាស៊ីណូប៉ោយប៉ែត ដែលជាមជ្ឈមណ្ឌលសេដ្ឋកិច្ចដ៏សំខាន់ កាលពីថ្ងៃទី 18 ខែធ្នូ។ ការកើនឡើងនៃជម្លោះនេះបានកើតឡើងខណៈដែលមហាអំណាចអន្តរជាតិ រួមមានចិន និងម៉ាឡេស៊ី បានបង្កើនកិច្ចខិតខំប្រឹងប្រែងផ្នែកការទូតដើម្បីបញ្ឈប់ការប្រយុទ្ធគ្នា។ ចិនបានប្រកាសថាខ្លួនកំពុងបញ្ជូនបេសកជនពិសេសសម្រាប់ការធ្វើដំណើរ 'ការទូតចម្លង' (shuttle-diplomacy) ដើម្បីផ្សារភ្ជាប់គម្លាតរវាងប្រទេសទាំងពីរ ខណៈដែលបណ្តាប្រទេសបរទេសបានដាក់សម្ពាធឱ្យភាគីទាំងសងខាងស្តារបទឈប់បាញ់ឡើងវិញ។

summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk expressed grave concern over the use of fighter jets, drones, and artillery near civilian villages and cultural sites. Cambodia has accused Thailand of bombing a casino complex in Poipet, a major border crossing. The UN reminded both nations of their obligations under the Ottawa Treaty regarding landmines and international humanitarian law to protect non-combatants, noting that nearly 800,000 people have been forced to flee the region.

summary: Strategic analysis indicates that the Thai-Cambodian tension is no longer a manageable bilateral issue but a indicator of the future security order in Southeast Asia. The conflict highlights ASEAN's decreasing relevance as it lacks the tools for arbitration. The dispute is becoming a state of 'militarized coexistence' where permanent insecurity is normalized, further complicated by the involvement of great powers like China and the U.S.

summary: Ongoing border clashes have displaced hundreds of thousands of civilians on both sides. In Thailand's Buriram province, about 15,000 residents from frontline villages are sheltering at the Chang International Circuit. Similar scenes are reported in Cambodia's Oddar Meanchey and Siem Reap provinces, where villagers are fleeing to relief centers as fighting intensifies and hits civilian areas. The total number of displaced persons is estimated at up to 800,000.

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held separate phone calls with his Cambodian and Thai counterparts on December 18. Both nations expressed a willingness to de-escalate tensions and move toward a ceasefire. China has dispatched a special envoy for 'shuttle-diplomacy' to both countries. Additionally, foreign ministers from both sides have agreed to meet in person in Kuala Lumpur on December 22 for an ASEAN-led meeting aimed at resolving the conflict.

Both nations expressed a willingness to de-escalate tensions and move toward a ceasefire. China has dispatched a special envoy for 'shuttle-diplomacy' to both countries. Additionally, foreign ministers from both sides have agreed to meet in person in Kuala Lumpur on December 22 for an ASEAN-led meeting aimed at resolving the conflict.

summary: China has initiated 'shuttle diplomacy' to mediate the escalating border conflict between Thailand and Cambodia, which the editorial describes as one of the most severe armed confrontations between ASEAN states since the Cold War. Beijing emphasizes that the conflict disrupts regional economic integration and mechanisms like the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation. China urges an immediate halt to the fighting to protect the shared interests of the region and create conditions for a political solution.

summary: The border conflict has spread to the Gulf of Thailand, with the Royal Thai Navy declaring 'high-risk zones' to intercept fuel and military supplies headed for Cambodia. This marks the first significant naval involvement in the five-month conflict. Thailand claims the move is a 'peaceful approach' to restrict Cambodia's military capacity, while reports indicate Cambodia has used drones to target Thai oil platforms. Clashes on land continue across multiple provinces with dozens killed.

summary: The US government has issued a travel advisory for Thailand and Cambodia, warning citizens to avoid travel within 50 kilometers of the border areas, specifically citing the provinces of Sisaket and Surin in Thailand, and Banteay Meanchey in Cambodia. The advisory follows a renewed outbreak of fighting on December 7, 2025, and reports of ongoing active hostilities and unpredictable cross-border fire.

The advisory follows a renewed outbreak of fighting on December 7, 2025, and reports of ongoing active hostilities and unpredictable cross-border fire.

summaryTh: รัฐบาลสหรัฐฯ ออกประกาศเตือนการเดินทางสำหรับประเทศไทยและกัมพูชา โดยแนะนำให้พลเมืองหลีกเลี่ยงการเดินทางในรัศมี 50 กิโลเมตรจากพื้นที่ชายแดน โดยเฉพาะในจังหวัดศรีสะเกษและสุรินทร์ของไทย และจังหวัดบันเตียเมียนเจยของกัมพูชา คำเตือนนี้มีขึ้นหลังจากการสู้รบระลอกใหม่ที่เริ่มขึ้นเมื่อวันที่ 7 ธันวาคม 2025 และมีรายงานเรื่องการยิงโต้ตอบกันข้ามพรมแดนที่ยังคงเกิดขึ้นอย่างต่อเนื่องและคาดเดาไม่ได้

summary: The U.S. Embassy has issued an urgent security alert for the border region due to continued cross-border fire and volatile conditions. U.S. citizens are advised to avoid all travel within 50 kilometers of the Thailand-Cambodia border. The embassy noted that the security situation remains unpredictable and government ability to provide emergency services in these areas is limited.

The embassy noted that the security situation remains unpredictable and government ability to provide emergency services in these areas is limited.

summary: The Cambodian Interior Ministry reported on Sunday that 518,611 people have been displaced due to two weeks of border clashes with Thailand. The conflict, which involves tanks, drones, and F-16 aircraft, has killed at least 22 people in Thailand and 19 in Cambodia. International bodies including the UN, US, and China have called for a ceasefire as ASEAN ministers prepare for a crisis meeting in Malaysia.

summary: Renewed fighting along the 800-kilometer border has displaced approximately 518,611 people in Cambodia and around 400,000 in Thailand. The Royal Thai Air Force has reportedly deployed F-16 fighter jets for airstrikes against military installations. Both nations trade accusations over the instigation of fighting, which centers on colonial-era border demarcations and ancient temple ruins.

summary: More than 518,000 Cambodians have been displaced due to two weeks of deadly border clashes with Thailand involving tanks, drones, and artillery. The conflict has killed at least 22 people in Thailand and 19 in Cambodia. Southeast Asian foreign ministers are scheduled to meet in Kuala Lumpur on December 22 to attempt to de-escalate tensions, though Thailand has demanded that Cambodia announce a truce first.

summaryTh: ชาวกัมพูชากว่า 518,000 คนต้องอพยพเนื่องจากการปะทะชายแดนที่รุนแรงกับไทยเป็นเวลา 2 สัปดาห์ซึ่งมีการใช้รถถัง โดรน และปืนใหญ่ การปะทะทำให้มีผู้เสียชีวิตอย่างน้อย 22 รายในไทย และ 19 รายในกัมพูชา รัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศอาเซียนมีกำหนดพบกันที่กัวลาลัมเปอร์ในวันที่ 22 ธันวาคม เพื่อพยายามลดความตึงเครียด แม้ว่าไทยจะเรียกร้องให้กัมพูชาเป็นฝ่ายประกาศพักรบก่อนก็ตาม

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul reported that Thai forces have taken control of nearly all target areas and are compelling Cambodian forces to withdraw. A spokesperson for the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the conflict has resulted in the deaths of 34 Thai civilians. Despite declining intensity, shellings were still reported in Sa Kaeo province on Sunday afternoon, and a Thai marine was injured by a landmine in Trat province.

summary: More than 500,000 people in Cambodia and 400,000 in Thailand have been displaced by two weeks of deadly border clashes. Fighting involving tanks, drones, and F-16 airstrikes has killed at least 22 people in Thailand and 19 in Cambodia. The conflict, rooted in colonial-era border disputes, continues daily despite international mediation efforts from the US and China. ASEAN foreign ministers are meeting in Kuala Lumpur today to find a diplomatic solution.

summary: The ASEAN Foreign Ministers held a special meeting in Kuala Lumpur to address the escalating hostilities between Cambodia and Thailand. The Chair urged both nations to cease hostilities immediately and fully implement the Kuala Lumpur Joint Declaration signed in October 2025. The meeting reaffirmed ASEAN's centrality in ensuring regional peace and supported the deployment of the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to verify any ceasefire arrangements.

summary: ASEAN foreign ministers have issued a collective call for 'maximum restraint' between Thailand and Cambodia. Analysts cited in the report suggest that trust between the two neighbors has fallen to a 'freezing point.' The upcoming December 24 meeting is viewed as a critical opportunity to de-escalate hostilities that have seen both sides exchange heavy artillery fire. China has expressed interest in continuing its role as a mediator alongside ASEAN.

summary: Following a special ministerial meeting, ASEAN members issued a call for the 'cessation of all forms of hostilities' between Thailand and Cambodia. The statement emphasized restoring mutual trust and returning to dialogue through bilateral mechanisms. The regional grouping seeks to promote immediate steps toward peace, with a follow-up military-level meeting scheduled for later this week to verify ceasefire implementation.

The regional grouping seeks to promote immediate steps toward peace, with a follow-up military-level meeting scheduled for later this week to verify ceasefire implementation.

summary: Official data released on Monday indicates significant casualties: Thailand reports 22 soldiers and 38 civilians killed. Heavy gunfire and artillery strikes were reported in Sa Kaeo and other border zones early Monday morning. Cambodia's Ministry of Interior also reported Thai use of artillery, tanks, and F-16 fighter jets, while both nations continue to blame each other for initiating the conflict that reignited on Dec 7.

summary: Malaysian Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, acting as ASEAN Chair, convened a special meeting in Kuala Lumpur to address the border situation. The ministers urged both nations to exercise maximum restraint and utilize the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) for military de-escalation. The meeting highlighted the need to revive cooperation on humanitarian demining and announced that the General Border Committee (GBC) will meet on Dec 24 to discuss ceasefire verification.

The ministers urged both nations to exercise maximum restraint and utilize the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) for military de-escalation. The meeting highlighted the need to revive cooperation on humanitarian demining and announced that the General Border Committee (GBC) will meet on Dec 24 to discuss ceasefire verification.

summaryTh: รัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศมาเลเซีย ดาตุก เซรี โมฮาหมัด ฮาซัน ในฐานะประธานอาเซียน ได้จัดประชุมนัดพิเศษที่กัวลาลัมเปอร์เพื่อแก้ปัญหาชายแดน โดยรัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศอาเซียนเรียกร้องให้ทั้งสองประเทศใช้ความอดกลั้นอย่างสูงสุดและใช้ทีมผู้สังเกตการณ์อาเซียน (AOT) เพื่อลดระดับความขัดแย้งทางทหาร นอกจากนี้ยังเน้นย้ำถึงความจำเป็นในการรื้อฟื้นความร่วมมือด้านการเก็บกู้ทุ่นระเบิดเพื่อมนุษยธรรม และประกาศว่าคณะกรรมการชายแดนทั่วไป (GBC) จะประชุมกันในวันที่ 24 ธันวาคม เพื่อหารือเรื่องการตรวจสอบการหยุดยิง

summary: The Thai Foreign Ministry stated that the October ceasefire was pushed too quickly by Washington to coincide with a presidential visit, contributing to its eventual collapse. Current reports indicate at least 74 deaths and over 510,000 displaced people as fighting enters its third week. Cambodia has accused Thai forces of firing artillery into civilian areas and using toxic gas, while Thailand claims Cambodia is laying new landmines.

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow revealed that the previous October ceasefire, witnessed by US President Donald Trump, failed because it was 'rushed' by Washington for political ceremony and lacked technical details for verification. Defense officials will now meet on December 24 to establish a 'true ceasefire' with a detailed implementation plan. Thailand emphasized that de-mining the border is essential for any progress, as recent landmine explosions have fueled mistrust between the two militaries.
summaryEn: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow revealed that the previous October ceasefire, witnessed by US President Donald Trump, failed because it was 'rushed' by Washington for political ceremony and lacked technical details for verification. Defense officials will now meet on December 24 to establish a 'true ceasefire' with a detailed implementation plan. Thailand emphasized that de-mining the border is essential for any progress, as recent landmine explosions have fueled mistrust between the two militaries.

summary: Thailand's foreign minister announced that Thailand and Cambodia would resume talks to work toward a durable ceasefire along their border. The decision followed a special ASEAN meeting in Kuala Lumpur, where ministers urged maximum restraint after weeks of combat that have killed over 80 people. The talks will involve the long-established General Border Committee (GBC) to verify ceasefire implementation, as previous truces brokered by Malaysia and US President Donald Trump have struggled to hold.
summaryEn: Thailand's foreign minister announced that Thailand and Cambodia would resume talks to work toward a durable ceasefire along their border. The decision followed a special ASEAN meeting in Kuala Lumpur, where ministers urged maximum restraint after weeks of combat that have killed over 80 people. The talks will involve the long-established General Border Committee (GBC) to verify ceasefire implementation, as previous truces brokered by Malaysia and US President Donald Trump have struggled to hold.

summaryTh: รัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศของไทยประกาศว่าไทยและกัมพูชาจะรื้อฟื้นการเจรจาเพื่อสร้างการหยุดยิงที่ยั่งยืนบริเวณชายแดน การตัดสินใจนี้มีขึ้นหลังจากการประชุมอาเซียนนัดพิเศษที่กัวลาลัมเปอร์ ซึ่งบรรดารัฐมนตรีได้เรียกร้องให้ใช้ความอดทนอดกลั้นสูงสุดหลังจากการสู้รบหลายสัปดาห์ทำให้มีผู้เสียชีวิตกว่า 80 ราย การเจรจาจะใช้กลไกคณะกรรมการชายแดนทั่วไป (GBC) เพื่อตรวจสอบการหยุดยิง เนื่องจากข้อตกลงก่อนหน้านี้ที่มาเลเซียและประธานาธิบดีโดนัลด์ ทรัมป์ ของสหรัฐฯ ช่วยประสานงานนั้นยังไม่สามารถรักษาสันติภาพไว้ได้

summary: Reports indicate that China is actively mediating the conflict, with its special envoy for Asian affairs, Deng Xijun, visiting Phnom Penh. The upcoming December 24 talks are expected to address the root causes of recent friction, including the deployment of heavy artillery and Cambodian accusations of Thai air strikes, while Thailand remains focused on landmine risks and border security.

summary: Following an emergency ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur, defense officials from Thailand and Cambodia agreed to convene on December 24 via the General Border Committee (GBC) to discuss a resumption of the ceasefire. The ongoing conflict, which intensified on December 7, has claimed at least 41 lives (22 in Thailand and 19 in Cambodia) and displaced over 750,000 people. While the ASEAN meeting itself did not produce an immediate truce, it facilitated the move toward bilateral military talks in Thailand's Chanthaburi province.
summaryEn: Following an emergency ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur, defense officials from Thailand and Cambodia agreed to convene on December 24 via the General Border Committee (GBC) to discuss a resumption of the ceasefire. The ongoing conflict, which intensified on December 7, has claimed at least 41 lives (22 in Thailand and 19 in Cambodia) and displaced over 750,000 people. While the ASEAN meeting itself did not produce an immediate truce, it facilitated the move toward bilateral military talks in Thailand's Chanthaburi province.

summary: Officials from Thailand and Cambodia are scheduled to meet on December 24 via the General Border Committee (GBC) to negotiate a potential ceasefire. This follows a special ASEAN meeting in Kuala Lumpur where Malaysia and China acted as mediators. Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow expressed that previous peace deals were rushed by the U.S. and lacked necessary implementation details, emphasizing that a true ceasefire requires rigorous verification.

summary: The Royal Embassy of Cambodia in France has issued a travel advisory warning citizens and international travelers against transiting through Bangkok. This move reflects the deepening diplomatic rift following the resumption of hostilities along the border, with Cambodia encouraging travelers to find alternative routes to Phnom Penh that bypass Thai territory.

summary: Following a special ASEAN meeting in Kuala Lumpur, Thailand and Cambodia have agreed to convene the General Border Committee (GBC) on December 24. The talks aim to revive a failed ceasefire as the conflict enters its third week. Reports indicate at least 80 people have been killed and hundreds of thousands displaced. Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow emphasized the need for a 'true ceasefire' with a detailed implementation plan, noting that previous attempts were rushed due to international pressure.

summary: Military officials from Thailand and Cambodia are scheduled to meet on December 24 to discuss reviving a ceasefire as the border conflict enters its third week. According to the report, at least 41 people have been killed and nearly one million civilians have been displaced since fighting resumed on December 7. The conflict is being described as the worst between ASEAN members since the bloc's founding in 1967. Thailand's Foreign Minister noted that previous ceasefire efforts were 'rushed' due to international pressure and emphasized the need for a deal that reflects the actual situation on the ground.

summary: Thailand and Cambodia have scheduled a high-level General Border Committee (GBC) meeting for December 27 to discuss a ceasefire. From December 24 to 26, negotiations under this mechanism are taking place at the secretariat level. ASEAN foreign ministers have welcomed these discussions and urged both nations to uphold their previous commitments to peace, specifically referencing the Kuala Lumpur Joint Declaration from October 2025 and the earlier July 28 ceasefire agreement.

summary: Military officials from Thailand and Cambodia have commenced talks to resume a ceasefire following border clashes that have claimed dozens of lives on both sides. The three-day GBC meeting in Thailand is intended to pave the way for a formal agreement between defense ministers on December 27. The talks follow a Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Kuala Lumpur and efforts to salvage a truce previously brokered by Malaysia and the United States.

summary: Officials from Thailand and Cambodia have begun four days of talks in Thailand's Chanthaburi province aimed at ending border clashes that have killed more than 40 people and displaced around one million. The meeting was delayed due to a disagreement over the venue, with Cambodia initially requesting a neutral site. The talks, organized under the General Border Committee (GBC) framework, are expected to continue through Saturday, with Bangkok expressing hope for a positive outcome if both sides show sincerity.
summaryEn: Officials from Thailand and Cambodia have begun four days of talks in Thailand's Chanthaburi province aimed at ending border clashes that have killed more than 40 people and displaced around one million. The meeting was delayed due to a disagreement over the venue, with Cambodia initially requesting a neutral site. The talks, organized under the General Border Committee (GBC) framework, are expected to continue through Saturday, with Bangkok expressing hope for a positive outcome if both sides show sincerity.
summaryKh: មន្ត្រីមកពីប្រទេសថៃ និងកម្ពុជា បានចាប់ផ្តើមការចរចារយៈពេល 4 ថ្ងៃ នៅក្នុងខេត្តចន្ទបុរី ប្រទេសថៃ ក្នុងគោលបំណងបញ្ចប់ការប៉ះទង្គិចគ្នានៅតាមព្រំដែន ដែលបានសម្លាប់មនុស្សជាង 40 នាក់ និងធ្វើឱ្យមនុស្សប្រហែល 1 លាននាក់ភៀសខ្លួន។ កិច្ចប្រជុំត្រូវបានពន្យារពេលដោយសារតែការមិនចុះសម្រុងគ្នាលើទីតាំង ដោយកម្ពុជាដំបូងឡើយបានស្នើសុំទីតាំងអព្យាក្រឹត។ ការចរចានេះធ្វើឡើងក្រោមក្របខ័ណ្ឌគណៈកម្មាធិការព្រំដែនទូទៅ (GBC) ហើយត្រូវបានគេរំពឹងថានឹងបន្តរហូតដល់ថ្ងៃសៅរ៍ ដោយទីក្រុងបាងកកសម្តែងក្តីសង្ឃឹមសម្រាប់លទ្ធផលវិជ្ជមាន ប្រសិនបើភាគីទាំងពីរបង្ហាញភាពស្មោះត្រង់។
summaryTh: เจ้าหน้าที่จากไทยและกัมพูชาเริ่มการเจรจาเป็นเวลา 4 วันในจังหวัดจันทบุรี เพื่อยุติการปะทะกันตามแนวชายแดนที่ทำให้มีผู้เสียชีวิตกว่า 40 คน และต้องอพยพผู้คนกว่า 1 ล้านคน การประชุมล่าช้าออกไปเนื่องจากความเห็นไม่ตรงกันเรื่องสถานที่ โดยกัมพูชาขอให้ใช้สถานที่ที่เป็นกลาง การเจรจาภายใต้กรอบคณะกรรมการชายแดนทั่วไป (GBC) จะดำเนินไปจนถึงวันเสาร์ ซึ่งกรุงเทพฯ หวังว่าผลการเจรจาจะเป็นบวกหากทั้งสองฝ่ายมีความจริงใจ

summary: The death toll in the border conflict has risen to 96 as the fighting enters its 18th day. Casualties include soldiers and civilians on both sides. Nearly one million people have been displaced since the escalation began on December 8. Military talks started on Wednesday in Chanthaburi, Thailand, with a high-level meeting scheduled for Saturday. Cambodia reported the death of a civilian from artillery shelling on Thursday, while Thailand reported rocket attacks hitting civilian infrastructure in Sa Kaeo.

Nearly one million people have been displaced since the escalation began on December 8. Military talks started on Wednesday in Chanthaburi, Thailand, with a high-level meeting scheduled for Saturday. Cambodia reported the death of a civilian from artillery shelling on Thursday, while Thailand reported rocket attacks hitting civilian infrastructure in Sa Kaeo.

summary: The second day of the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting in Chanthaburi was marked by tension after Cambodian Defense Minister Tea Seiha denied reports that Cambodia had sent a letter requesting a ceasefire. He attributed the confusion to incorrect translations by Thai media and AI tools. Meanwhile, Thai caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul stated that Thailand's actions were a response to being attacked and urged patience for the GBC outcome, while Thailand has reportedly laid out three non-negotiable conditions for a lasting peace.

summary: A World Food Programme (WFP) report indicates that market functionality has weakened sharply in December 2025 due to the border conflict. Seven markets have closed, and while basic food costs have actually fallen due to decreased demand and seasonal factors, the persistence of clashes threatens long-term food security and supply chain stability for vulnerable households and displacement camps.

summary: The total death toll from the border conflict between Thailand and Cambodia has risen to 96 as of Thursday. Nearly one million people have been displaced on both sides since fighting reignited on December 8. Cambodia reported 31 civilian deaths, while Thailand reported 23 soldiers and 42 civilian deaths (including collateral effects). Military talks are ongoing in Chanthaburi province, with a high-level meeting co-chaired by defense ministers scheduled for Saturday.

summary: Reporting on the deep distrust between the neighbors, this article highlights that Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet spoke with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about securing a ceasefire. Despite diplomatic interventions from the US, China, and Malaysia, the conflict over the 800km frontier and temple ruins has intensified. summary: Cambodia has accused Thai forces of conducting 'ruthless' aerial attacks on Friday morning, specifically targeting the village of Chouk Chey with dozens of bombs. The Cambodian Defence Ministry described the strikes as 'grave acts of aggression' that damaged civilian property and infrastructure. The violence occurred while both nations were engaged in talks intended to de-escalate the border conflict that has killed 96 people since December 8.

summary: Thai Defense Minister Natthaphon Narkphanit and Cambodia's Defense Minister Tea Seiha are expected to hold high-level talks in Thailand's Chanthaburi province on Saturday. summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that the National Security Council has authorized the Defence Minister to meet his Cambodian counterpart on Saturday, December 27. The goal is to reach a deal based on a previous October pact, which includes mine-clearing, withdrawing heavy weapons, and allowing ceasefire monitors. Anutin mentioned that if a 72-hour ceasefire is maintained, Thailand will consider releasing 18 Cambodian prisoners of war captured in previous clashes.

Anutin mentioned that if a 72-hour ceasefire is maintained, Thailand will consider releasing 18 Cambodian prisoners of war captured in previous clashes.

summary: Cambodia accused the Thai military of dropping as many as 40 bombs using F-16 fighter jets on Chok Chey village in Banteay Meanchey province on Friday morning. Meanwhile, Thai media reported that Cambodian forces launched heavy attacks overnight in Sa Kaeo province, damaging several homes. Despite the escalation, the defense ministers of both countries are scheduled to meet on Saturday, December 27, to negotiate an end to the fighting, which has killed over 40 people and displaced around 1 million civilians.

summary: Thailand and Cambodia agreed on Saturday to halt weeks of fierce border clashes, the worst in years. The joint statement, signed by Thai Defense Minister Natthaphon Narkphanit and Cambodian counterpart Tea Seiha, went into effect at noon. Both sides committed to maintaining current troop deployments without further movement to avoid heightening tensions. The fighting, which included fighter jet sorties and artillery exchanges, has killed at least 101 people and displaced over half a million since early December.

summary: Thailand and Cambodia signed a ceasefire agreement on Saturday, December 27, to end 20 days of fierce border clashes. The agreement, signed by Thai Defence Minister Natthaphon Narkphanit and Cambodian counterpart Tea Seiha, took effect at noon local time. It mandates that both sides maintain current troop deployments without further movement to prevent heightening tensions. The conflict has resulted in at least 101 deaths and the displacement of over 500,000 people on both sides.

summary: The new ceasefire agreement signed at a border checkpoint includes 16 de-escalation measures. Key terms include a ban on military airspace violations and a commitment to repatriate 18 Cambodian prisoners of war held since July, provided the truce holds for 72 hours. The agreement also addresses the use of land mines and cooperation against transnational cybercrime. Thailand reported 26 military and 45 civilian deaths (including collateral effects) since Dec 7, while Cambodia reported 30 civilian deaths.

summary: The deal, signed at a border checkpoint, includes 16 de-escalation measures. Since December 7, Thailand reported 26 soldiers and 45 civilians dead, while Cambodia reported 30 civilian deaths. The agreement paves the way for displaced families to return home and children to resume school. It also calls for joint demining operations and a commitment to stop the spread of fake news that could inflame tensions.

summary: The ceasefire agreement calls for an end to combat, no further military movements, and no violations of airspace for military purposes. Thai defense ministry spokesperson Rear Admiral Surasant Kongsiri confirmed the truce was holding two hours after it began but noted the first 72 hours are an 'observation period' to prove commitment. The agreement also includes adherence to landmine treaties and will be monitored by an ASEAN observer team.

summary: Thai Defence Minister Nattaphon Narkphanit and Cambodian counterpart Tea Seiha signed a ceasefire agreement on December 27 at a border checkpoint. The pact ended 20 days of fighting that utilized fighter jets and heavy artillery. The agreement includes the return of 18 Cambodian soldiers held by Thailand, provided the truce holds for 72 hours, and allows displaced civilians to return home.
summaryEn: Thai Defence Minister Nattaphon Narkphanit and Cambodian counterpart Tea Seiha signed a ceasefire agreement on December 27 at a border checkpoint. The pact ended 20 days of fighting that utilized fighter jets and heavy artillery. The agreement includes the return of 18 Cambodian soldiers held by Thailand, provided the truce holds for 72 hours, and allows displaced civilians to return home.

summary: The new deal, effective Dec 27 at noon, requires a freeze on troop movements and prohibits provocative actions. A key condition involves Thailand releasing 18 Cambodian soldiers held since July, provided the truce holds for 72 hours. An ASEAN observer team will monitor implementation. Thai officials cited 26 soldiers and 45 civilians killed (including collateral), while Cambodia reported 30 civilian deaths and 90 injuries.

summary: China has invited the Foreign Ministers of Thailand and Cambodia to Yunnan for a trilateral meeting from Sunday to Monday. Military representatives from all three nations will participate to discuss long-term stability. The Chinese government welcomed the December 27 ceasefire, which was mediated with the support of the UN and ASEAN. The meeting aims to build on the current de-escalation efforts.

summary: A new ceasefire took effect at noon on December 27 following weeks of fighting that killed at least 47 people and displaced around one million civilians. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged both sides to honor the commitment to the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accords, while the EU and UN welcomed the news. The agreement also covers demining and suppressing transnational cybercrime.

The deal also addresses transnational cybercrime and joint demining efforts.

summary: Thailand and Cambodia signed a joint agreement on December 27 at the 3rd special meeting of the General Boundary Committee (GBC) to halt all hostilities. The agreement includes 16 de-escalation measures, such as a ban on troop movements and provocations. After a 72-hour sustained ceasefire, Thailand is committed to returning 18 Cambodian soldiers held in custody. Both nations reaffirmed obligations under the Ottawa Convention regarding anti-personnel mines.

summary: Thailand and Cambodia agreed to an 'immediate' ceasefire on Saturday, pledging to end border clashes that killed dozens and displaced over a million people. The UN Secretary-General and US Secretary of State welcomed the move. The truce, signed at a border checkpoint, involves a freeze on troop movements and a 72-hour observation period. Thailand committed to returning 18 captured Cambodian soldiers if the peace holds.

Thailand committed to returning 18 captured Cambodian soldiers if the peace holds.

summary: Top diplomats from Thailand and Cambodia began two days of talks in Yunnan, China, on Sunday, mediated by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. The report also notes that Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow is a candidate in Thailand's upcoming February elections.

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow and Cambodian counterpart Prak Sokhonn met in Yunnan, China, for talks mediated by Wang Yi. The discussions aimed to ensure the sustainability of the new ceasefire, which includes a 72-hour observation period and the potential release of 18 captured Cambodian soldiers by Thailand. China is positioning itself as a primary mediator alongside the US and Malaysia.
summaryEn: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow and Cambodian counterpart Prak Sokhonn met in Yunnan, China, for talks mediated by Wang Yi. The discussions aimed to ensure the sustainability of the new ceasefire, which includes a 72-hour observation period and the potential release of 18 captured Cambodian soldiers by Thailand. China is positioning itself as a primary mediator alongside the US and Malaysia.
summaryKh: រដ្ឋមន្ត្រីការបរទេសថៃ លោក ស៊ីហាស័ក្តិ ភួងកេតកែវ និងសមភាគីកម្ពុជា លោក ប្រាក់ សុខុន បានជួបគ្នានៅខេត្តយូណាន ប្រទេសចិន ក្រោមការសម្របសម្រួលរបស់លោក វ៉ាង យី។ ការពិភាក្សានេះមានគោលបំណងធានានូវនិរន្តរភាពនៃការឈប់បាញ់ថ្មី ដែលរួមមានរយៈពេលសង្កេតការណ៍ 72 ម៉ោង និងលទ្ធភាពនៃការដោះលែងទាហានកម្ពុជា 18 នាក់ដែលថៃចាប់ខ្លួន។ ប្រទេសចិនកំពុងដាក់ខ្លួនជាអ្នកសម្របសម្រួលចម្បង រួមជាមួយសហរដ្ឋអាមេរិក និងម៉ាឡេស៊ី។
summaryTh: นายสีหศักดิ์ พวงเกตุแก้ว รัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศของไทย และนายปรัก สุคน รัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศกัมพูชา ได้พบกันที่มณฑลยูนนาน ประเทศจีน โดยมีนายหวัง อี้ เป็นคนกลาง การหารือมุ่งเน้นที่การทำให้การหยุดยิงมีความยั่งยืน ซึ่งรวมถึงช่วงเวลาสังเกตการณ์ 72 ชั่วโมง และความเป็นไปได้ที่ไทยจะปล่อยตัวทหารกัมพูชา 18 นายที่ถูกจับกุม ทั้งนี้จีนกำลังวางบทบาทเป็นตัวกลางหลักร่วมกับสหรัฐฯ และมาเลเซีย

He expressed appreciation for the mediation efforts of ASEAN chair Malaysia, China, and the United States. The UN statement reiterated readiness to support efforts aimed at maintaining regional stability.

The UN statement reiterated readiness to support efforts aimed at maintaining regional stability.

summary: Cambodia sent a diplomatic note to Thailand proposing a Joint Commission on Demarcation for Land Boundary (JBC) meeting in Siem Reap during early January 2026. The goal is to resume survey work and achieve 'lasting border peace' after air strikes and military clashes in December displaced hundreds of thousands of civilians.
summaryKh: កម្ពុជាបានផ្ញើកំណត់ទូតទៅកាន់ប្រទេសថៃ ដោយស្នើឱ្យមានកិច្ចប្រជុំគណៈកម្មការចម្រុះខណ្ឌសីមាព្រំដែនគោក (JBC) នៅខេត្តសៀមរាប នាដើមខែមករា ឆ្នាំ 2026។ គោលបំណងគឺដើម្បីបន្តការងារវាស់វែង និងសម្រេចបាននូវ 'សន្តិភាពព្រំដែនយូរអង្វែង' បន្ទាប់ពីការវាយប្រហារតាមអាកាស និងការប៉ះទង្គិចគ្នាផ្នែកយោធាកាលពីខែធ្នូ បានធ្វើឱ្យជនស៊ីវិលរាប់សែននាក់ផ្លាស់ទីលំនៅ។

summary: Following 20 days of conflict that claimed 101 lives and displaced 500,000 people, Thailand and Cambodia signed a ceasefire on Dec 27. The agreement includes a commitment to freeze troop movements. Analysts suggest the conflict was exacerbated by nationalist posturing in Thailand under PM Anutin Charnvirakul to boost polling. China reportedly pressured both sides into the truce as U.S. mediation efforts failed to prevent the second outbreak of war this year.
summaryEn: Following 20 days of conflict that claimed 101 lives and displaced 500,000 people, Thailand and Cambodia signed a ceasefire on Dec 27. The agreement includes a commitment to freeze troop movements. Analysts suggest the conflict was exacerbated by nationalist posturing in Thailand under PM Anutin Charnvirakul to boost polling. China reportedly pressured both sides into the truce as U.S. mediation efforts failed to prevent the second outbreak of war this year.
summaryKh: បន្ទាប់ពីជម្លោះរយៈពេល 20 ថ្ងៃ ដែលបានសម្លាប់មនុស្ស 101 នាក់ និងធ្វើឱ្យមនុស្ស 500,000 នាក់ភៀសខ្លួន ប្រទេសថៃ និងកម្ពុជាបានចុះហត្ថលេខាលើកិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងឈប់បាញ់គ្នានៅថ្ងៃទី 27 ខែធ្នូ។ កិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងនេះរួមបញ្ចូលទាំងការប្តេជ្ញាចិត្តក្នុងការបង្កកចលនាទ័ព។ អ្នកវិភាគយល់ថា ជម្លោះនេះត្រូវបានធ្វើឱ្យកាន់តែធ្ងន់ធ្ងរឡើងដោយជំហរជាតិនិយមនៅក្នុងប្រទេសថៃ ក្រោមការដឹកនាំរបស់នាយករដ្ឋមន្ត្រី អានុទីន ឆានវីរៈកុល ដើម្បីបង្កើនប្រជាប្រិយភាព។ តាមសេចក្តីរាយការណ៍ ចិនបានដាក់សម្ពាធលើភាគីទាំងសងខាងឱ្យឈប់បាញ់គ្នា ខណៈដែលកិច្ចខិតខំប្រឹងប្រែងសម្របសម្រួលរបស់សហរដ្ឋអាមេរិកបានបរាជ័យក្នុងការទប់ស្កាត់ការផ្ទុះសង្គ្រាមលើកទីពីរក្នុងឆ្នាំនេះ។
summaryTh: หลังจากความขัดแย้งเป็นเวลา 20 วันซึ่งคร่าชีวิตผู้คนไป 101 รายและทำให้มีผู้พลัดถิ่น 500,000 คน ไทยและกัมพูชาได้ลงนามในข้อตกลงหยุดยิงเมื่อวันที่ 27 ธันวาคม ข้อตกลงดังกล่าวรวมถึงคำมั่นที่จะระงับการเคลื่อนไหวของกองกำลัง นักวิเคราะห์คาดว่าความขัดแย้งรุนแรงขึ้นจากการแสดงจุดยืนชาตินิยมในไทยภายใต้การนำของนายกฯ อนุทิน ชาญวีรกูล เพื่อกระตุ้นคะแนนนิยม มีรายงานว่าจีนได้กดดันทั้งสองฝ่ายให้ทำข้อตกลงหยุดยิง เนื่องจากความพยายามไกล่เกลี่ยของสหรัฐฯ ล้มเหลวในการป้องกันการเกิดสงครามครั้งที่สองในปีนี้

summary: In an emotional broadcast from China, Cambodian FM Prak Sokhonn emphasized the historical and social ties between border communities. He stressed that both nations have 'no choice but to live together peacefully' and highlighted the need to restore normal trade and livelihoods that existed before the December escalation.

summary: Cambodia’s State Secretariat of Border Affairs sent a diplomatic note to Thailand proposing a Joint Commission on Demarcation for Land Boundary (JBC) meeting in Siem Reap during the first week of January 2026. The goal is to resume demarcation work to ensure lasting peace. Thailand's foreign ministry later responded that conditions may not yet be met due to its caretaker government status and widespread landmines.

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi hosted a two-day meeting in Yunnan ending Dec 29 with the foreign ministers of Thailand and Cambodia. The talks aimed to consolidate the Dec 27 ceasefire. China pledged support for de-mining and the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT).

summary: While diplomatic talks proceed in China, Thailand has raised concerns regarding fresh ceasefire violations allegedly committed by Cambodian forces. summary: Families in Pailin province are still waiting for the return of 18 soldiers held by Thailand for 154 days. Cambodia has urged immediate repatriation as per the terms.

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi hosted an urgent trilateral meeting with his Thai and Cambodian counterparts in Yuxi on December 29. The meeting resulted in a three-point consensus focused on looking ahead, making steady incremental progress, and rebuilding mutual trust following the December 27 ceasefire. Wang Yi emphasized that both Southeast Asian nations are committed to de-escalating and improving relations after weeks of deadly border clashes.

summary: Soldiers were repatriated at a border checkpoint between Thailand's Chanthaburi and Cambodia's Pailin province. summary: Thailand released 18 Cambodian soldiers on Wednesday (Dec 31) following a ceasefire agreement signed on Dec 27. The soldiers, held for 155 days since July, were repatriated at a border checkpoint after a 72-hour ceasefire observation period. The deal ended 20 days of heavy fighting that killed at least 101 people and displaced over 500,000. The handover was briefly delayed as Thailand investigated alleged drone violations by Cambodia.

The soldiers, held for 155 days since July, were repatriated at a border checkpoint after a 72-hour ceasefire observation period. summaryKh: ប្រទេសថៃបានដោះលែងទាហានកម្ពុជាចំនួន 18 នាក់ កាលពីថ្ងៃពុធ (31 ធ្នូ) បន្ទាប់ពីមានកិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងឈប់បាញ់ដែលបានចុះហត្ថលេខាកាលពីថ្ងៃទី 27 ធ្នូ។ ទាហានទាំងនោះដែលត្រូវបានឃុំខ្លួនអស់រយៈពេល 155 ថ្ងៃ តាំងពីខែកក្កដា ត្រូវបានបញ្ជូនត្រឡប់មកវិញតាមច្រកព្រំដែន បន្ទាប់ពីរយៈពេលសង្កេតការណ៍ឈប់បាញ់ 72 ម៉ោងបានបញ្ចប់។ កិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងនេះបានបញ្ចប់ការប្រយុទ្ធគ្នាដែលអូសបន្លាយពេល 20 ថ្ងៃ ដែលបានសម្លាប់មនុស្សយ៉ាងហោចណាស់ 101 នាក់ និងធ្វើឱ្យមនុស្សជាង 500,000 នាក់ត្រូវភៀសខ្លួន។ ការប្រគល់ខ្លួននេះមានការយឺតយ៉ាវបន្តិចបន្តួច ដោយសារភាគីថៃធ្វើការស៊ើបអង្កេតលើការចោទប្រកាន់រឿងយន្តហោះដ្រូនរបស់កម្ពុជាដែលបានហោះចូលទឹកដីថៃ។
summaryTh: ประเทศไทยได้ปล่อยตัวทหารกัมพูชา 18 นายเมื่อวันพุธ (31 ธ.ค.) ตามข้อตกลงหยุดยิงที่ลงนามเมื่อวันที่ 27 ธ.ค. ทหารเหล่านี้ถูกควบคุมตัวไว้นานถึง 155 วันตั้งแต่เดือนกรกฎาคม และได้รับการส่งตัวกลับที่ด่านชายแดนหลังจากผ่านช่วงเฝ้าระวังการหยุดยิง 72 ชั่วโมง ข้อตกลงนี้ช่วยยุติการสู้รบอย่างหนักตลอด 20 วันที่ผ่านมา ซึ่งส่งผลให้มีผู้เสียชีวิตอย่างน้อย 101 รายและประชาชนกว่า 500,000 คนต้องอพยพ ทั้งนี้การส่งตัวล่าช้าไปเล็กน้อยเนื่องจากไทยต้องตรวจสอบข้อกล่าวหาเรื่องการใช้โดรนรุกล้ำจากฝั่งกัมพูชา
